subject: Archive-to-Wipe timeline and proof-of-erasure options
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novapulse.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 +02:00
Subject: Archive-to-Wipe timeline - initial Qs

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we sync with legal and infra at NovaPulse, a couple of items came up that we need clarified before we can sign the order form:

1) We plan to keep archived conversational data for 180 days in hot storage, then move to an immutable archive for another 3 years. At the end of the archive period we need a certifiable final wipe. Can Redwood commit to a "final erase" timeline in the SLA and what does certification look like?

2) If we choose cryptographic key-slicing / customer-managed keys, how does that affect the delete timing and proof?

3) Our lawyers want the order form to list discrete retention windows per dataset class (PII transcripts, telemetry, embeddings). Is Redwood able to support per-dataset windows on a per-customer basis?

I've attached our requirements doc. Can you send a short, annotated option set (SLA language + timelines) that we can attach to our procurement packet?

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Senior Privacy Counsel
NovaPulse Health

Attachment: NovaPulse-Requirements-20261015.pdf

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novapulse.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Archive-to-Wipe timeline - initial Qs

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list; copied Neha (Compliance) to keep the answers tight. High level answers below and I attached a short draft we typically use for bespoke windows.

Summary options we can put into the order form (pick one or mix-and-match per dataset class):
- Option A (Standard): Hot retention 30/90/180 days, archive retention up to 3y. Final wipe execution: within 30 days after archive expiry; customer receives deletion certificate within 7 days of execution.
- Option B (Accelerated): Final wipe execution within 7 days after archive expiry; certificate within 48 hours.
- Option C (Customer-managed KMS): We perform deletion of object data within 24 hours of erasure command; final cryptographic key destruction/rotation managed on your KMS schedule (we can trigger key revocation on your instruction). Certificate issued after verification of both object deletion and KMS crypto-erase.

Per-dataset windows: Yes — we can capture per-dataset retention windows (e.g., PII transcripts = 180d hot + 365d archive; embeddings = 30d hot + 90d archive). These are stored as order form line-items and enforced by our routing layer and data lifecycle agent.

Proof of deletion we offer:
- Deletion manifest (object IDs + time) exported as CSV
- SHA256-based existence check that shows objects were removed from the active store
- Audit log extract showing API calls and worker job completion
- An optional signed certificate (PDF) generated by our Compliance team that references the job IDs and timestamps.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached Redwood draft (redwood-bespoke-windows-v1.docx) and mark preferred options per dataset.
2) We'll bake the selections into the order form and push a DocuSign link.

Happy to jump on a 20m call if you want to walk legal through the technical bits.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
D +1 415-555-0194

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novapulse.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 16:42:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Archive-to-Wipe timeline - initial Qs

Elena / Matt —

Answers inline:

- Manifest/hash retention: By default, manifests and audit-log extracts are retained for 90 days to support troubleshooting and compliance requests. If you require shorter retention for those artifacts, we can add a clause to the order form to purge manifests within X days (X = 0/7/30). Note: certificate documents (PDF) are retained for 7 years by Redwood under our evidence retention policy unless otherwise negotiated. We can make certificate retention configurable in the order form.

- KMS / non-repudiation: For Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed key storage. In those configurations:
  * Redwood never stores unencrypted key material.
  * Crypto-erase can be triggered by NovaPulse via the KMS control plane (we support automatic triggers or customer-initiated revocation).
  * We can include explicit wording in the order form: "Customer retains sole possession and control of key material; Redwood will not retain any backup of key material once the key is revoked/destroyed."

Technical notes: final erase step includes both object-level deletion (S3 lifecycle job + background shard GC) and an optional cryptographic key destruction step (where enabled). The certificate references both job IDs (redwood-job-XXXXX) and timestamps. Audit logs include worker checksums and worker node IDs.

I've drafted suggested order form text and marked the KMS clause — see attached order form draft. If this aligns, we can update pricing sheet and push to DocuSign.

Best,
Diego

Attachment: redwood-orderform-draft-20261020.docx
